{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABXtnrhQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhBR-jY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 15, "title": "Complete WebXR DOM Overlay implementation for Android AR and Quest 3 MR", "body": "## Problem

[Issue #13](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/issues/13) was administratively closed after the partial [PR #14](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/pull/14) merged. **That PR completed feasibility investigation and argument validation, not DOM Overlay support.** Reopening #13 is not desired; **this new Issue tracks all outstanding production implementation and acceptance work**. Do not treat the previous Issue's closed state or prototype successes as completion.

The production emulator **does not advertise `dom-overlay` in any mode**: required-feature requests reject with `NotSupportedError`, optional ones are omitted, and `XRSession.domOverlayState` remains `null`. Neither the Android phone nor Quest MR has a supported live overlay presentation or integrated XR/DOM interaction.

## Expected outcome

Implement usable, standards-aligned WebXR DOM Overlay support in the production extension for BOTH currently supported AR/MR configurations:

1. **Generic Android Phone (ARCore), `immersive-ar`**: project the application's **original live DOM overlay** onto the moving virtual phone XR screen, preserving interactive HTML controls, CSS layout, hit targets, root identity, input, and viewport alignment.
2. **Meta Quest 3, `immersive-ar` (MR)**: present the **same live overlay root** in both stereo XR eye views with correct per-eye geometry/disparity and usable controller-based DOM interaction. Select a standards-defined overlay type (`head-locked` or `floating`) only if actual rendering and input geometry justify that type.

For each supported profile/mode, implement correct `requiredFeatures`/`optionalFeatures`, `domOverlay.root`, `XRSession.domOverlayState`, `beforexrselect` cancellation, DOM input, cross-origin protection, and session lifecycle. Preserve the existing TypeScript, Three.js r186, Manifest V3, device modes, XR API modules, and tests.

**Feature honesty is mandatory.** Do not enable or advertise `dom-overlay` where complete presentation+input is unavailable. If a browser-level limitation prevents the Quest implementation, record tested proof and viable alternatives, **leave the corresponding requirement unchecked and this Issue open**. Do not substitute a cloned, non-interactive second DOM tree, a detached desktop overlay, custom CSS emulating native `:xr-overlay`, or the test-only prototype as evidence of compliance.

## Context

- This is the production follow-up to closed [Issue #13](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/issues/13) and partial [PR #14](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/pull/14), and addresses unfinished DOM Overlay scope from [Issue #11](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/issues/11)/[PR #12](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/pull/12).
- Start with [feasibility findings](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/dom-overlay-feasibility.md), [recorded experiments](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/dom-overlay-validation-2026-10-16.json), and the **test-only** `tests/dom-overlay-prototype.ts`. The Android prototype showed live DOM `matrix3d` projection, native click/focus, and <=2 CSS-pixel alignment under pose/DPR changes; this is **not yet production code**.
- The Quest prototype's two-eye `cloneNode(true)` approach **failed** to retain root identity, event listeners, focus, and synchronized live input state. DOM Elements are not valid ordinary canvas `drawImage` sources; current stable Chromium lacked the probed HTML-in-Canvas element paint methods. `:xr-overlay` was parsed but did not match the emulated element. Avoid assuming that a Three.js `HTMLTexture` class alone provides browser DOM capture. Investigate an available same-root alternative, possibly browser-assisted HTML-in-Canvas as an **experimental feasibility path**, with version/flag requirements explicitly documented; do not require experimental browser flags in the standard release unless a supported deployment strategy exists.
- Code of interest: `src/polyfill/api/runtime.ts`, `src/polyfill/EmulatedXRDevice.ts`, `src/polyfill/ARScene.ts`, `src/polyfill/api/layers.ts`, `src/types/polyfill.ts`, `src/app/panel.ts`, `tests/conformance.ts`, `tests/browser-smoke.ts`.
- Use the latest applicable published [WebXR DOM Overlays Module](https://www.w3.org/TR/webxr-dom-overlays-1/) (24 September 2024 Working Draft at the previous investigation), pin revision/requirements, and follow the repo's [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/review-guidelines.md), and PR template. Author Issue/PR/commits in English, implement from `dev`, and target `dev`.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] **Implement Android production rendering** based on the researched live DOM projection: arbitrary supplied connected overlay root, correct viewport layout/transparent compositing, native click/focus/form controls and scrolling where supported, clipping/occlusion, and transformation with the virtual phone/camera. Verify visual alignment and real hit targets during translation, rotation, DPR 1/2, active resizing, and display changes.
- [ ] **Implement a viable Quest MR stereo solution** that projects a *single live application DOM root* consistently to left/right views, respects overlay transform/eye disparity, avoids divergent clones/state, and supports pointer/controller targeting and real interactive controls. Confirm its actual `head-locked` or `floating` geometry and render order. Provide explicit repeatable evidence before enabling the feature.
- [ ] **Implement correct public API and feature negotiation:** `XRSessionInit.domOverlay.root` conversion and ownership/document checks; required/optional behavior; `session.enabledFeatures`; stable, truthful `session.domOverlayState.type` when enabled; `null` otherwise. Validate malformed, missing, disconnected, foreign-document, SVG, and cross-realm roots with appropriate errors and no side effects. Never advertise support for unsupported modes (e.g. Quest VR or inline).
- [ ] **Implement `beforexrselect` and XR/DOM input interaction:** intersect actual displayed overlay hit targets using Android transient screen touch and Quest controller rays; emit appropriate bubbling, composed, cancelable `XRSessionEvent` on the correct topmost target, suppress the entire relevant `selectstart`/`selectend`/`select` sequence when canceled, and preserve native DOM pointer/click/focus and unaffected XR input. Test event order, held input, entry/exit of hit targets, and shutdown during handlers.
- [ ] **Secure cross-origin interactions:** adopt and document a specification-permitted restriction, e.g. conservatively block XR-derived overlay interaction targeting embedded browsing contexts where origin/sandbox/navigation cannot be classified safely. Test same-origin descendants, cross-origin iframe, nested/sandbox/opaque frames, navigation, and entering/leaving those hit regions. Avoid XR pose/gamepad leakage and privileged bridge expansion.
- [ ] **Evaluate real CSS semantics and clearly disclose limits:** verify `:xr-overlay` selector matching, UA/top-layer/backdrop behavior, focus and ancestor styling in the target browser. A custom class/attribute is not full native CSS conformance; do not assert full standards compliance when the browser cannot expose the needed UA state. Record supported behavior and mismatches with links to spec sections.
- [ ] **Cover lifecycle and coexistence:** overlay active at session start; clean up on `session.end()`, device or Quest VR/MR switch, page reload, root removal/move, visibility changes, window resizing, and worker suspension. Restore original DOM placement and inline styles; remove added listeners/resources. Preserve Layers, Hit Test, depth/anchors/hand input, CSP-safe MAIN-world startup, cross-frame routing and Firefox packaging.
- [ ] **Add strong reproducible tests** in `tests/conformance.ts` and real-unpacked-extension browser tests; include positive/negative API negotiation, native DOM inputs, accurate overlay pixels/geometry in actual phone and BOTH Quest eye images, cancelable events, security, resize/DPR, session transitions and cleanup. Include a real WebXR DOM Overlay sample or explain any blocked sample. Extend WPT coverage where executable and distinguish passing subset from full compliance.
- [ ] Run and report the *actual* results of `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:firefox`, `npm run test:browser`, plus relevant `npm run test:wpt` and `npm run test:samples` on a current desktop Chrome/Chromium. Document test browser/build, visual evidence, supported modes, browser-only limitations, failures/skips and any Firefox runtime not tested.
- [ ] Update README, `docs/webxr-conformance.md`, and a DOM Overlay implementation/validation report to show **verified** supported/unsupported configurations, rendering approaches, known CSS/browser constraints, security decisions, and reproductions. Keep the production feature disabled per mode until its visual/input acceptance tests pass.
- [ ] Create focused PR(s) targeting `dev` with the repo PR template and appropriate review; **do not close this Issue merely because a partial PR is merged**. All mandatory Android and Quest production acceptance criteria must be achieved and validated before claiming this Issue is complete; otherwise clearly report the remaining work and leave it open.

## Optional validation

- Firefox MV3 runtime/DevTools testing when a supported Firefox installation is available.
- Complex responsive overlays, shadow DOM/custom elements, accessibility/keyboard behavior, and real-device visual comparison.
- Independently test an emerging HTML-in-Canvas/browser-assisted texture approach on a supported experimental browser build, without representing its gated behavior as production support.

## Required post-merge verification

None. All acceptance checks required for completion are pre-merge checks; release-store publication and physical hardware certification are outside this Issue.
